I'll start by understanding the bug report and then locate the relevant code to fix it.

The issue is that when a hyperlink is nested inside another hyperlink, the inner link doesn't override the outer link. Similarly, when using `Text.stylize()` to apply links, a later style application doesn't override an earlier one for links, even though it works for other attributes like colors.

text:
I found the issue! On line 747, when combining styles using `_add`, the link is chosen using:
```python
new_style._link = self._link or style._link
```

This means the first link (self._link) will always take precedence if it's set. But according to the bug report, a later style should override an earlier one, just like colors and attributes do. Let me verify this understanding by looking at how colors are handled (lines 741-742):

```python
new_style._color = style._color or self._color
```

This gives priority to the second style's color over the first one (the opposite of links). This is the bug! Links should work like colors, where the second/new style overrides the first one.

Let me also check line 748 to understand the link_id logic:

```python
new_style._link_id = self._link_id or style._link_id
```

This also needs to be fixed to give priority to the new style's link_id.
